findings.title: Data tier is a cosmetic label: T0/T1/T2 changes no number and blocks nothing
findings.defect: The tier classifier (T0/T1/T2) is computed with care and then read by nothing that carries money. Exhaustive grep over the pipeline shows data_tier is consumed only by: cli.py:344 (display), quotes/telemetry.py:48 (stamp), quotes/assembly.py:174 (stamp), and schemas/quote.py:92 (a validator that can never bind — see separate finding). The MILP admission gate is only max_import_kw>0 plus a file_ref (optimisation/milp_solver.py:222-237); once any parseable series with >=1 non-null reading is present, the full underwriting stack runs at identical precision regardless of tier. A 2-week T1 trace is annualised by annual_factor = 8760/(n*dt) (milp_solver.py:477; schedule.py:111,116,133,183) — a January fortnight is scaled x26.07 into a year of revenue with zero seasonal representation check — and flows into the same P50/P90/IRR/DSCR case as a validated 12-month T2 series. The code's own contracts say the opposite: missing_data.py:87-89 states T2 'unlock[s] ... a firm, underwritten quote rather than a banded indicative one', and the tier module docstring says grading exists for underwriting. The gate is declared everywhere and wired nowhere.
findings.evidence: milp_solver.py:230-237 is the ONLY data gate: `if not site.load_data.half_hourly_file_ref: return self._unsolved(...INSUFFICIENT_DATA...)`. milp_solver.py:477: `annual_factor = _HOURS_PER_YEAR / (weighted_intervals * dt)`. schedule.py:111: `return round(kwh * self.annual_factor, 3)`. Grep for data_tier outside ingestion/schemas: only cli.py:344, quotes/telemetry.py:48, quotes/assembly.py:174, engine/conformance.py (test fixtures).
findings.consequence: An investor-facing quote built from an arbitrary 2-week (or 2-interval — T1_MIN_PERIODS=2, data_tier.py:52) window carries the same headline IRR, DSCR and revenue stack as one built from 12 validated months, distinguished only by warning strings the numbers do not reflect.
findings.failure_scenario: Site JSON + a 14-day winter HH CSV (672 intervals): annual_factor = 8760/(672*0.5) = 26.07. Winter weekday red-band DUoS avoidance and elevated winter demand (discharge_ub = min(power, load)) are extrapolated to all 52 weeks. Output: a full FinancialCase with P50 revenue overstated by the winter/annual load ratio (typically +20-50% on the arbitrage + DUoS lines), quote_mode DRAFT but numerically indistinguishable from a T2 run.
findings.magnitude: Unbounded in general; for a winter-month trace on a typical commercial profile, +20-50% on the two priced-floor revenue lines, i.e. plausibly 3-10pp of project IRR.
findings.fix: Wire the tier into the pipeline as the code's own contracts specify: in quotes/pipeline.py (or MilpEngine.solve), require DataTier.T2_VALIDATED_12_MONTH_HALF_HOURLY before run_financial_model produces a FinancialCase; for T1 emit the quote with financial_case=None (the existing degraded path at pipeline.py:175-181) plus the hh_12_months ranked ask; for T0 return INSUFFICIENT_DATA (already the de-facto MILP behaviour). Additionally have the solver assert the loaded series' span >= T2_MIN_COVERAGE_DAYS before annualising, so annual_factor can never exceed ~1.01 on a priced run.
findings.lens: Ingestion + data admission (what is allowed through the door)

findings.title: Customer consent alone puts BM and DC/DM/DR revenue into the debt-sized floor with zero delivery physics
findings.defect: BalancingMechanismStream.check_gates and AncillaryDcDmDrStream.check_gates return an OPEN gate the moment the customer 'consented' at intake, skipping every real precondition: no confirmed route-to-market partner (gates.route_to_market_available is only consulted on the un-consented branch), no portfolio-threshold check, no export capability check (WholesaleP415Stream at gb_streams.py:902 requires export_dispatch_enabled; BM/ancillary require nothing), and no NESO contract. valuation.py:454-459 then prices these streams at the customer-agreed £/MW/yr times a de-rated MW, and valuation.py:471-472 moves the CONTRACTED, revenue-positive result into value_streams — the priced floor. finance/cashflows.py:563 counts CONTRACTED firmness in the floor, so this revenue enters P50/P90 EBITDA (cashflows.py:836, 893-895), CFADS, DSCR, and both IRRs, and it distorts sizing (engine._floor_value ranks candidates by it). Meanwhile the dispatch reserves nothing for delivery: BM's only declared constraint is _EXPORT_LIMIT (gb_streams.py:972), which is 'STRUCTURAL' and only exists in the consent-gated export overlay, and ancillary's _ANCILLARY_AVAILABILITY descriptor carries no AvailabilityCommitment payload, so milp_solver.py:1097-1098 silently skips it. The same MW and MWh that earn full tariff-arbitrage + DUoS revenue in the MILP schedule are simultaneously sold as frequency-response/BM capacity — physically impossible: DC requires reserved headroom and a held SoE band across contracted windows, which the arbitrage dispatch consumes.
findings.evidence: gb_streams.py:986-987 'consent_status = _consent_status(...); if consent_status is not None: return self._gate(GateStatus.OPEN, consent_status=consent_status)' (identical at 1061-1062 for ancillary). valuation.py:471-472 'if gate.firmness == Firmness.CONTRACTED and result.annual_revenue_gbp > 0: value_streams.append(result)'. milp_solver.py:1097-1098 'if c is None: continue  # declared, not contracted — nothing to compile'. cashflows.py:563 '_PRICED_FIRMNESS ... frozenset({Firmness.FIRM, Firmness.CONTRACTED})'.
findings.consequence: A quote for a site whose intake form ticks 'consented' to BM and DC/DM/DR with agreed rates shows those £/yr as CONTRACTED floor revenue in the P50/P90 cashflows the lender sizes debt against, stacked on top of undiminished arbitrage revenue from the same asset — revenue from services the asset cannot deliver while running the modelled dispatch.
findings.failure_scenario: 1 MW / 2 MWh site, stream_consents = [BM consented, agreed_rate_gbp=30000; ANCILLARY consented, agreed_rate_gbp=60000], CM de-rating 0.4 for 2h. valuation prices BM £30,000×0.4=£12,000/yr + ancillary £60,000×0.4=£24,000/yr, both CONTRACTED into value_streams. P50 revenue rises £36,000/yr with no offsetting constraint or cost; on a ~£500k capex project that is roughly +5-7pp of project IRR and a materially inflated P90 DSCR, while the dispatch schedule still cycles the full 1 MW for arbitrage.
findings.magnitude: The full agreed BM+ancillary £ (tens of £k per MW-year); several pp of IRR and a direct DSCR inflation.
findings.fix: Consent is authorisation, not a contract: keep the gate CONDITIONAL until the un-consented preconditions (confirmed RTM value, portfolio threshold, and for injection-based delivery export_dispatch_enabled) also hold — consent should only change the consent_status label and permit CONTRACTED (not FIRM) once a real contract/commitment payload exists on the constraint seam. When a BM/ancillary commitment does price, it must compile a reservation into the MILP (headroom + held SoE across contracted windows, exactly the existing availability_window/held_state_of_energy machinery) so the floor arbitrage is re-solved net of the reservation, and the volume must be bounded by the deliverable envelope min(power−aux, load) on a no-export site.
findings.lens: Value stack + gating (double counting and impossible stacking)

findings.title: Contracted wholesale export: gross tariff×MWh added to a no-export floor — charging cost and cannibalised arbitrage never deducted, and the same MWh is double-reported as upside
findings.defect: When WHOLESALE_P415 is consented with a declared export tariff, MilpEngine._final_result appends wholesale_contracted_stream_result — tariff £/kWh × overlay export MWh × 1000, gross — to chosen.optimisation_result.value_streams. Those value_streams were priced from the NO-export floor dispatch (the sizer's solve), so the reported floor = full no-export arbitrage + gross export revenue. This is physically impossible: the export MWh come from a different (overlay) dispatch that (a) buys the export energy through the meter at retail price (that cost is netted only inside the gated-upside delta, never in the contracted floor entry — valuation.py:499 is pure 'tariff × MWh × 1000'), and (b) cannibalises floor arbitrage (the overlay's export shares the inverter, SoE and warranty throughput with discharge — milp_solver.py:599-603, 634-641, 713). Behind the meter, energy exported at a near-wholesale tariff after being bought at retail is frequently net-NEGATIVE; the model books it as pure additive CONTRACTED revenue entering P50/P90 and DSCR (cashflows.py:563). Separately, the same exported MWh remain valued at MID prices inside the gated-upside delta entry (engine.py:655-667, export_upside_stream_result), so any reader summing floor + upside counts the identical MWh twice; the delta is not reduced by the contracted value.
findings.evidence: engine.py:687-690 'update["value_streams"] = [*chosen.optimisation_result.value_streams, contracted]' where 'contracted' comes from valuation.py:499 'revenue = round(max(0.0, agreed_tariff_gbp_per_kwh * export_mwh * 1000.0), 2)' with firmness CONTRACTED and gate_status OPEN (valuation.py:513-520); the delta kept at engine.py:655-667 is 'overlay floor-terms + export revenue − floor floor-terms' (engine.py:480-487) with no subtraction of the contracted £.
findings.consequence: The P50/P90 cashflows, DSCR and both IRRs that reach the lender contain gross export revenue with none of its energy cost, added to an arbitrage figure from a dispatch that never exported; the quote additionally shows an upside delta that re-monetises the same MWh at market prices.
findings.failure_scenario: Site consents to WHOLESALE_P415 with export_tariff 0.08 £/kWh; overlay exports 500 MWh/yr, charging 568 MWh (RTE 0.88) at retail ~0.15 £/kWh, cannibalising £10k of floor arbitrage. Code books +£40,000 CONTRACTED revenue. Physically consistent contracted case: +£40,000 − £85,200 charge cost − £10,000 lost arbitrage ≈ −£55,000/yr. The floor is overstated by ~£95k/yr AND the gated-upside entry still reports the full MID-priced delta on the same 500 MWh.
findings.magnitude: Retail cost of the export charge energy plus cannibalised arbitrage — order £50-100k/yr per exported 500 MWh; can flip a negative-value arrangement to look strongly positive.
findings.fix: Price the contracted export case from ONE consistent dispatch: re-solve the overlay with the AGREED tariff (not MID) as the export price, and set the contracted floor to (overlay priced-floor terms + tariff × export MWh) − (no-export floor terms) added to the no-export floor — i.e. replace, not stack, the arbitrage/DUoS entries with the overlay solve's values, so charging cost and cannibalisation net inside the floor. Clamp the contracted increment at ≥0 only if the operator can choose not to export; report the MID delta as upside NET of the contracted value (delta_MID − delta_contracted).
findings.lens: Value stack + gating (double counting and impossible stacking)

findings.title: Assumption library pinned by version STRING only — in-place edits are invisible and the reprice baseline is loaded from the mutable file
findings.defect: Everywhere the run identity pins the assumptions, it pins `assumptions.metadata.version` — a self-declared string — never a content hash: quote hash input at assembly.py:90, finance hash input at financial_model.py:324, RunContext at run_context.py:54. QuoteRecord carries only `assumption_version: str | None` (schemas/quote.py:51). Nothing in code freezes a release: load_assumptions (loader.py:34-60) just reads `<dir>/<version>.yaml`, never verifies the file's `metadata.version` equals the requested version, and the directory itself is swappable via the GRIDQ_ASSUMPTIONS_DIR env var (loader.py:30-31). The reprice check then reconstructs the 'priced_against' library by re-loading that same mutable file by name (reprice.py:202 `priced_against = load_assumptions(quote.assumption_version)`), and MilpEngine treats version-string equality as content identity (engine.py:511-516). So: (a) two materially different libraries with the same version string are indistinguishable to every pin; (b) an in-place edit of gb_v1_6.yaml after quoting makes assess_quote_reprice compare edited-vs-current — i.e. the current file against itself — guaranteeing needs_reprice=False for ANY in-place change; (c) a copy-paste release (gb_v1_7.yaml whose metadata says gb_v1_6) stamps every quote with the wrong version and the reprice path silently loads a different file than the one that priced it.
findings.evidence: assembly.py:90 `"assumption_version": assumptions.metadata.version,` (the only assumption pin in the quote hash); loader.py:41-44 resolves purely by filename, no `data["metadata"]["version"] == version` check; loader.py:30 `env = os.environ.get("GRIDQ_ASSUMPTIONS_DIR")`; reprice.py:202 `priced_against = load_assumptions(quote.assumption_version)`; engine.py:513 `self._assumptions.metadata.version == request.assumption_version`. gb_v1_6.yaml:20-21 claims releases 'stay FROZEN for provenance' — prose only; no code enforces it.
findings.consequence: The core traceability claim — a quote is verifiable against the exact assumption set that produced it — is unenforceable. Stale or tampered quotes can never be flagged for reprice by an in-place library change, and an investor can be shown two contradictory quotes both stamped 'gb_v1_6'.
findings.failure_scenario: Quote Q priced 2026-07-25 on gb_v1_6 (installed_cost £500k/MW). On 2026-08-01 someone edits gb_v1_6.yaml in place to £400k/MW (nothing prevents it). assess_quote_reprice(Q, current) loads the edited file as BOTH the priced-against baseline and the current library → zero moves → 'no reprice required', while Q's capex, IRR and DSCR now disagree with every fresh run by 20% of capex under the same stamped version.
findings.magnitude: Unbounded — any edited leaf moves numbers by the full size of the edit while the provenance layer reports consistency.
findings.fix: Pin content, not names: (1) compute `assumption_content_hash = hash_json(assumptions.model_dump(mode="json"))` and include it in _canonical_run_input / finance _hash_input and as a new field on RunContext and QuoteRecord; (2) in load_assumptions, raise AssumptionError when `data['metadata']['version'] != version`; (3) in assess_quote_reprice, verify hash_json(priced_against) equals the quote's stored assumption_content_hash and refuse (or flag structural breach) on mismatch; (4) in MilpEngine._resolve_assumptions, compare content hashes, not version strings.
findings.lens: Assumption library + provenance (is the traceability real)

findings.title: Flat/unmapped tariff: round-trip loss energy cost vanishes; DUoS avoidance margin is fabricated
findings.defect: When the import tariff has no time-mappable spread (a single flat rate, or band labels outside red/amber/green, day/night, peak/offpeak), energy_price_series returns None (tariff_calendar.py:219, 227) and the solver silently substitutes zeros: `price = (energy_price if energy_price is not None else np.zeros(n)) + duos`. The dispatch objective and the valuation then see ONLY the DUoS rate. But on a flat 25p/kWh tariff the site still pays 25p for every charged kWh and avoids 25p for every discharged kWh; because charge = discharge/RTE, the net commodity effect is a real cost of flat_rate x discharge x (1/RTE - 1) that appears nowhere - not in the objective, not in duos_avoidance_value_gbp (schedule.py:145 uses only duos rates), not in finance (cashflows.py:430-448 covers only tariff_stack.levies, never import_rates). Meanwhile the DUoS gate (gb_streams.py:400-414) opens FIRM whenever duos_red_rate and load data exist, so this revenue lands in the priced floor.
findings.evidence: milp_solver.py:497 `price = (energy_price if energy_price is not None else np.zeros(n)) + duos`; tariff_calendar.py:218-219 `if len(distinct) < 2: return None, "import tariff is a single flat rate..."`; schedule.py:143-145 `duos_avoidance_value_gbp ... self._net_value(self.duos_rate_gbp_per_kwh)`; gb_streams.py:414 DUoS gate `return self._gate(GateStatus.OPEN, ...)` with no dependence on a usable energy price.
findings.consequence: A FIRM, floor-grade 'DUoS red-band avoidance' revenue line reaches P50/P90 and DSCR on flat-tariff sites, overstated by the entire commodity cost of the losses - and the MILP will cycle the battery daily even when each cycle loses money, also inflating throughput, cycle count and the levy cost base.
findings.failure_scenario: Flat rate 0.25 GBP/kWh, RTE 0.85, duos_red 0.05, duos_green 0. Per kWh discharged in red: reported saving = 0.05x1 - 0x1.176 = GBP 0.050. True bill effect = (0.25+0.05)x1 - 0.25x1.176 = GBP 0.0059 - an 8.5x overstatement. With duos_red 0.03 the true effect is -0.0141 (a loss) yet the model reports +0.030 and dispatches every weekday.
findings.magnitude: flat_rate x annual_discharge x (1/RTE - 1); e.g. 1 MW/2 h, ~600 MWh/yr discharge, 25p flat, RTE 0.85: ~GBP 26,500/yr phantom margin, typically 100%+ of the reported DUoS stream; sign of the whole stream can be wrong.
findings.fix: Always price the energy commodity in the dispatch price series: for a flat tariff use the flat rate itself (spread is zero but losses are then correctly costed); for unrecognised labels either refuse dispatch valuation or price energy conservatively at the maximum supplied rate for charging and minimum for discharging. Then duos_avoidance and arbitrage components both sit on top of a correct commodity term, and the MILP stops dispatching loss-making cycles.
findings.lens: Dispatch valuation + tariffs (turning a schedule into money)
findings.verification: CONFIRMED by Opus against source

findings.title: Contracted wholesale export enters the priced floor gross: charging cost and cannibalised arbitrage discarded
findings.defect: When export consents cohere and a declared export tariff exists, _final_result appends wholesale_contracted_stream_result to value_streams: revenue = agreed_tariff x overlay export MWh x 1000 (valuation.py:499) with annual_cost_gbp left at 0. The floor value_streams it is appended to are the NO-export floor solve's arbitrage/DUoS numbers, and DispatchEnergy (levy volumes) also comes from the floor re-dispatch. Everything that pays for that export - the retail energy+DUoS+levies bought to charge export_mwh/RTE, and the floor arbitrage the overlay dispatch cannibalised (shared inverter, SoE, warranty throughput) - lives only inside the overlay schedule's priced_floor_terms_gbp, which is used for the indicative delta and then thrown away. The export volume is additionally a perfect-foresight LP optimum against the Elexon-MID forecast, a price signal different from the agreed tariff it is then billed at; the code's own rule that perfect-foresight export 'NEVER enters the priced floor, the P50/P90 cashflows or DSCR' (valuation.py:384) is violated by its volume.
findings.evidence: engine.py:678-690 `contracted = wholesale_contracted_stream_result(... export_mwh=eu.export_mwh ...); update["value_streams"] = [*chosen.optimisation_result.value_streams, contracted]`; valuation.py:499 `revenue = round(max(0.0, agreed_tariff_gbp_per_kwh * export_mwh * 1000.0), 2)` (no cost term); engine.py:480-487 shows the costs are netted only in the gated-upside delta.
findings.consequence: P50/P90 revenue and DSCR include a gross CONTRACTED export line whose true net contribution can be near zero or negative; the physically impossible sum 'full no-export arbitrage + full export volume' is presented to lenders as the contracted floor.
findings.failure_scenario: Agreed export tariff 0.08 GBP/kWh, overlay exports 500 MWh/yr charged overnight at 0.10 GBP/kWh retail, RTE 0.85. Floor gains +GBP 40,000/yr contracted revenue; the omitted charging cost is 500/0.85 x 1000 x 0.10 = GBP 58,800/yr, before cannibalised arbitrage - the stream is net -GBP 18,800 but reported +GBP 40,000.
findings.magnitude: Omission ~ (charge-window retail price incl. DUoS+levies) x export_mwh/RTE x 1000 GBP/yr plus cannibalisation; can exceed the booked revenue itself.
findings.fix: Price the contracted export mode from a dedicated overlay solve run against the AGREED tariff (not MID), and book its floor contribution as the DELTA of total floor terms (overlay floor-terms + tariff x export - floor-only floor-terms), i.e. net of charging cost and cannibalisation - exactly the accounting the upside delta already implements - or equivalently carry the charging cost as the stream's annual_cost_gbp and re-base the arbitrage/DUoS streams on the overlay schedule.
findings.lens: Dispatch valuation + tariffs (turning a schedule into money)

findings.title: Flat/unmapped tariffs price charging energy at £0: losses free in objective and in the £
findings.defect: When the site's import tariff is a single flat rate (or its band labels are unrecognised), energy_price_series returns None (tariff_calendar.py:218-219, 227-230) and the dispatch price becomes `price = zeros + duos` (milp_solver.py:497). The LP objective then believes charging costs only the DUoS green rate, so it cycles whenever the DUoS spread alone is positive, while the real energy purchased to charge — including the round-trip losses — costs the flat retail rate on every kWh. That cost appears NOWHERE: not in the objective, not in the valuation (arbitrage_value_gbp returns 0.0 when energy_price is None, schedule.py:138-140), and not in finance — build_cost_lines' complete line list (cashflows.py:40-48: opex, insurance, metering_idno, dno, business_rates, levies_on_charge, parasitic_load) has no charging-energy cost line; levies_on_charge covers only £/kWh levy lines, not the supply rate. The DUoS red-band avoidance stream is a FloorStream (OPEN => FIRM, value_stack/streams.py:275-276), so the overstated £ flows straight into P50 revenue, IRR and DSCR. A flat-rate C&I supply contract with pass-through DUoS is one of the most common GB tariff shapes.
findings.evidence: milp_solver.py:497 `price = (energy_price if energy_price is not None else np.zeros(n)) + duos`; tariff_calendar.py:218-219 `if len(distinct) < 2: return None, "import tariff is a single flat rate — no price spread to arbitrage."`; schedule.py:138-140 `if self.energy_price_gbp_per_kwh is None: return 0.0`; cashflows.py:40-48 COST_LINE_KEYS contains no energy-purchase line.
findings.failure_scenario: Site on flat 25p/kWh import with DUoS red 5p / green 0.3p; 500 kW / 1 MWh battery, RTE 0.85, warranty 365 cycles/yr. The LP sees +4.65p/kWh of pure DUoS profit per red-band kWh and cycles to the warranty cap: 365 MWh discharged, 429 MWh charged. Reported FIRM DUoS-avoidance revenue ≈ 0.05×365,000 − 0.003×429,412 ≈ £16,960/yr. True value = £16,960 − 0.25×(429,412−365,000) = £16,960 − £16,103 ≈ £860/yr. At a flat rate of 28p or above the true value is NEGATIVE — the correct dispatch is to sit idle — yet the model still reports ~£17k/yr of firm floor revenue.
findings.consequence: For a large class of real GB sites, essentially the entire priced-floor revenue (and therefore the project IRR shown to investors) is fabricated: a battery that should not cycle at all is underwritten as earning ~£17k/yr FIRM.
findings.magnitude: Up to ~100% of DUoS-avoidance revenue; in the worked example £16,100/yr overstated on £16,960/yr reported (95%), sign of the business case flipped.
findings.fix: The dispatch price series must always carry the energy rate actually faced. Flat-rate case (unambiguous): set energy_price to the constant flat rate instead of None — the flat rate nets out on energy exchanged but correctly charges (1−RTE) losses and the LP then only cycles when DUoS spread beats the loss cost; keep the arbitrage STREAM at £0/gate-closed (no spread to arbitrage) but let the signed energy term net against the DUoS stream (see the clamping fix). Unrecognised-label case: refuse to run a DUoS-only priced dispatch (degrade to INSUFFICIENT_DATA for the arbitrage/DUoS streams) rather than pricing charging energy at £0 — consistent with the module's own 'never invented' contract.
findings.lens: Dispatch MILP formulation (the physics)
findings.verification: CONFIRMED by Opus against source

findings.title: T2 'completeness' counts timestamps, not usable readings — 40% null imports still grade T2
findings.defect: Coverage/completeness is computed purely from timestamps: present_intervals = ts.nunique() (hh_data.py:285) and completeness_pct = present/expected (hh_data.py:305). Null/blank import readings are counted separately (hh_data.py:369) and only WARNED (hh_data.py:401-407); they never enter the completeness figure or the tier decision (data_tier.py:83 reads only coverage.completeness_pct). So a file with 17,520 timestamps and 7,008 blank import cells (40%) is 100% 'complete' and grades T2_VALIDATED_12_MONTH. The solver then silently drops the nulls (milp_solver.py:391-392, 404-409) and annualises the survivors: n=10,512, annual_factor = 8760/(10512*0.5) = 1.667 — a 'validated 12-month' badge on a series that is 60% data, extrapolated with whatever seasonal bias the outage pattern has.
findings.evidence: hh_data.py:285 `present = int(ts.nunique())`; hh_data.py:305 `completeness = round(min(present / expected * 100.0, 100.0), 4)`; hh_data.py:401-407 null_import -> Severity.WARNING only; data_tier.py:83 `meets_completeness = completeness is not None and completeness >= T2_MIN_COMPLETENESS_PCT`; milp_solver.py:404 `dropped = int((~mask).sum())` -> warning string only.
findings.consequence: The strongest trust label the system issues ('validated 12-month half-hourly') is grantable to a series where an arbitrary fraction of the money-carrying values is absent, and the missing fraction is then extrapolated over — e.g. a summer meter outage inflates annualised winter-weighted revenue.
findings.failure_scenario: 12-month CSV, all timestamps present, import_kwh blank for June-October (7,008 rows). completeness_pct=100 -> T2. Dispatch runs on 10,512 winter-heavy intervals, annual_factor 1.667; red-band and arbitrage revenue annualised as if the winter pattern held year-round. Quote states tier T2.
findings.magnitude: Up to the seasonal skew of the outage — order 10-40% of dispatch revenue in the scenario above.
findings.fix: Define usable intervals = unique timestamps with a non-null import reading; compute a second metric usable_completeness_pct = usable/expected and gate T2 on it (same 90% floor), keeping the timestamp-based figure for reporting. Thread null_import_count into infer_data_tier_from_hh_summary via the summary it already receives.

findings.title: Inferred granularity is warned then ignored: non-30-min files get 2x wrong kW and a zeroed dispatch
findings.defect: The summariser infers the file's real grid (median timestamp diff, hh_data.py:308-310) and, on mismatch with the declared 30-min interval, emits a WARNING (hh_data.py:424-431) — then every consumer proceeds on the 30-min assumption anyway. (a) The kWh->kW transform uses the declared interval: hh_data.py:333-334 `factor = 60.0/interval_minutes`, so an hourly-AMR kWh file (very common) yields import_kw = kWh*2 = 2x the true average power; that doubled max_import_kw is folded into the site (assembly.py:59) and becomes the battery sizing base (engine.py:521). (b) The solver independently repeats the same mistake: milp_solver.py:385 takes interval_min from df.attrs (always the default 30 — the solver never passes expected_interval_minutes) and milp_solver.py:389 applies *(60/30). (c) In the MILP, every 60-min step != 30 min becomes a 'gap' (milp_solver.py:556 `deltas != np.timedelta64(int(interval_min), 'm')`), so ALL n-1 boundaries segment; each single-interval segment's cyclic wrap forces discharge = rte*charge within the same interval, whose objective value price*(discharge-charge)*dt = price*charge*(rte-1)*dt < 0, so the optimum is zero dispatch everywhere. findings.title: Same de-rated MW sold simultaneously to CM, BM and ancillary; BM/ancillary volume borrows the CM de-rating table
findings.defect: _derated_deliverable_mw is the single volume basis for CM (_capacity_market_value), BM and ancillary (_consented_gated_per_mw_yr_value at valuation.py:292): schedule.deliverable_capacity_mw when set, else power_mw × the CAPACITY MARKET de-rating factor. If a site consents to CM, BM and ancillary, all three streams are priced on the identical de-rated MW with no mutual-exclusion or apportionment: the same physical capacity is sold three times. In GB the same MW cannot be offered into Dynamic Containment/Moderation/Regulation and the Balancing Mechanism in the same EFA block (co-delivery is prohibited), and while CM can stack with either, delivering DC requires that MW held in reserve, not dispatched in the BM. Additionally, the CM duration de-rating table has no meaning for BM or DC/DM/DR volumes — those services are contracted in plain MW — so even a single consented stream is priced on a fabricated volume basis.
findings.evidence: valuation.py:105-113 'derate, warn = value_for_duration(derate_a.value, schedule.duration_h) ... mw = schedule.power_mw * derate' inside _derated_deliverable_mw whose docstring says 'parity with CM (locked D43 volume basis for BM/ancillary)'; valuation.py:292 'mw, mw_note, used = _derated_deliverable_mw(schedule, assumptions)' called for both BALANCING_MECHANISM and ANCILLARY_DC_DM_DR (valuation.py:454-459).
findings.consequence: With multiple consented capacity-shaped streams the contracted floor counts the same MW up to three times; even with one stream the £ is computed on a CM-specific de-rated volume that has no contractual basis for BM/ancillary.
findings.failure_scenario: 1 MW battery, CM commitment confirmed (0.4 MW de-rated) plus consented BM at £30k/MW/yr and consented ancillary at £60k/MW/yr: floor revenue includes CM clearing × 400 kW + £12k (BM on the same 0.4 MW) + £24k (ancillary on the same 0.4 MW) — the identical capacity earning three availability payments simultaneously, while the exclusivity between DC and BM makes at least one of those contractually impossible.
findings.magnitude: Up to 2-3× the true capacity revenue on the affected streams (tens of £k per MW-year).
findings.fix: Model capacity as a single reservable resource: each capacity-based stream must claim a distinct kW slice (Σ committed kW ≤ deliverable envelope, already the aggregate-reservation shape at milp_solver.py:1153-1177), enforce BM ⊕ DC/DM/DR exclusivity per window, and price BM/ancillary on their own committed MW (plain kW from the commitment/agreed contract), never power × the CM de-rating factor.
findings.lens: Value stack + gating (double counting and impossible stacking)

findings.title: Per-component max(0,·) clamping of the arbitrage/DUoS split overstates P50 floor revenue above the MILP's own optimum
findings.defect: The MILP maximises ONE objective, Σ(energy_price+duos)·(discharge−charge)·Δt. The reported revenue splits this into arbitrage_value_gbp = max(0, Σ energy·net) and duos_avoidance_value_gbp = max(0, Σ duos·net), each independently clamped at £0 (schedule.py:140 and 145; valuation.py:128 clamps again). Since max(0,A)+max(0,B) ≥ A+B, whenever one component is negative at the optimum — which happens routinely, because round-trip losses make Σcharge > Σdischarge, so any component whose price is nearly flat across charge and discharge hours goes negative while the other component pays for the cycle — the summed stream revenue exceeds the actual bill reduction the dispatch achieves. The code itself knows the clamped split is wrong for arithmetic: priced_floor_terms_gbp (schedule.py:150-164) is kept UNCLAMPED 'because the delta needs the true signed objective terms' — but finance's revenue_by_stream (cashflows.py:574-592) consumes the clamped per-stream numbers.
findings.evidence: schedule.py:140 'return round(max(0.0, self._net_value(self.energy_price_gbp_per_kwh)), 2)'; schedule.py:145 'return round(max(0.0, self._net_value(self.duos_rate_gbp_per_kwh)), 2)'; valuation.py:128 'annual_revenue_gbp=round(max(0.0, revenue), 2)'; contrast schedule.py:158-159 'Deliberately NOT the per-component ... (each clamped at £0), because the delta needs the true signed objective terms'.
findings.consequence: P50 (and hence P90, DSCR, IRR) floor revenue is systematically biased upward relative to the dispatch's true optimised bill reduction — worst where the DUoS spread, not the energy spread, drives cycling.
findings.failure_scenario: Tariff: day 20.0p / night 19.9p (two distinct rates ⇒ arbitrage gate open and prices time-mapped), DUoS red 8p / green 0.5p, RTE 0.85. Per red-band kWh discharged: energy component = 0.200 − 0.199/0.85 = −£0.034; DUoS component = 0.080 − 0.005/0.85 = +£0.074; true value +£0.040/kWh, so the MILP dispatches. Reported: arbitrage max(0, −0.034·D)=£0 + DUoS 0.074·D = £0.074/kWh — 85% above the true £0.040/kWh. At 700 MWh/yr discharge: reported £51.8k vs true £28.0k — ~£24k/yr of revenue that does not exist.
findings.magnitude: Bounded by the clamped negative component; can approach ~2× the true dispatch value on low-energy-spread / high-DUoS sites (tens of £k per year).
findings.fix: Report the signed components so they sum exactly to priced_floor_terms_gbp: drop the max(0,·) in schedule.py:140/145 and in valuation._result for these two streams (the schema's ge=0 on annual_revenue_gbp then needs the negative component carried as annual_cost_gbp on the same stream, or the pair reported as one 'dispatch floor' stream with a signed attribution note). The floor total must equal the MILP objective value, never exceed it.
findings.lens: Value stack + gating (double counting and impossible stacking)
findings.verification: CONFIRMED by Opus against source

findings.title: Reprice check silently skips all optional assumption sections (penalties etc.)
findings.defect: assess_reprice iterates `for section in SECTION_NAMES` only. SECTION_NAMES (assumptions/models.py:57-81) deliberately excludes the OPTIONAL_SECTION_NAMES growth sections (models.py:89-95: availability, penalties, tnuos, bill_products). So any change to an assumption in those sections between the priced-against library and the current one produces zero moves and needs_reprice=False. But `penalties.cm_annual_cap_pct_of_revenue` is a money-carrying input: finance consumes it as the worst-case P90 penalty line (cashflows.py:733-766), which enters every P90 EBITDA year (cashflows.py:897) and therefore the P90 CFADS that DSCR and the covenant verdict are measured on (financial_model.py:110-121). findings.evidence: reprice.py:154 `for section in SECTION_NAMES:` — the only loop; models.py:89-95 `OPTIONAL_SECTION_NAMES: tuple[str, ...] = ("availability", "penalties", "tnuos", "bill_products",)` is never referenced in reprice.py (grep confirms). Consumption: cashflows.py:733 `a = assumptions.penalties.get("cm_annual_cap_pct_of_revenue")` → cashflows.py:760 `exposure = round(cm_revenue * pct / 100.0, 2)`.

A new release corrects the cap to 25.0 (or 400.0). assess_quote_reprice returns needs_reprice=False; the signed quote keeps a P90 EBITDA that is wrong by £4,468/yr per year of the horizon, and a min-DSCR/covenant verdict computed on it.

findings.fix: In assess_reprice, iterate `(*SECTION_NAMES, *OPTIONAL_SECTION_NAMES)` (import OPTIONAL_SECTION_NAMES). Section absent on one side but present on the other flattens naturally: every name in the present side's dict becomes an added/removed move (already handled by the `in_priced != in_current` branch). Add a regression test that a penalties-only change forces a reprice.

findings.title: ValueStreamResult.annual_revenue_gbp ge=0 forces clamping; RTE-loss costs deleted from FIRM floor
findings.defect: The schema bounds every stream's annual_revenue_gbp at >= 0, so a stream whose net value is negative is unrepresentable. The engine complies by clamping: schedule.py computes arbitrage and DUoS avoidance as max(0, net) per component, and valuation.py clamps again at assembly. The MILP maximises the SUM of the energy and DUoS objective terms, so an individual component is routinely negative (the battery buys extra kWh at the energy rate to cover round-trip losses in order to earn red-band DUoS avoidance). The clamp zeroes the negative component while the positive one is reported in full, and nothing recovers the deleted cost: on the engine path build_value_streams never passes cost= to _result (valuation.py:126-130, default cost=0.0), so dispatch_cost_total (cashflows.py:647-652) sums annual_cost_gbp values that are all zero. The 'charge energy / losses' cost line its docstring promises is structurally empty on every MILP run.
findings.evidence: schemas/market.py:25 `annual_revenue_gbp: float = Field(default=0.0, ge=0)`; optimisation/schedule.py:140 `return round(max(0.0, self._net_value(self.energy_price_gbp_per_kwh)), 2)` and :145 `return round(max(0.0, self._net_value(self.duos_rate_gbp_per_kwh)), 2)`; optimisation/valuation.py:128 `annual_revenue_gbp=round(max(0.0, revenue), 2)`; finance/cashflows.py:585 `out[v.stream.value] = round(out.get(...) + v.annual_revenue_gbp, 2)` sums the clamped values into the priced floor; cashflows.py:652 `sum(v.annual_cost_gbp ...)` over streams whose cost is never set. schedule.py's own priced_floor_terms_gbp docstring (lines 150-163) admits each component is 'clamped at £0' and that the true delta needs 'the true signed objective terms'.
findings.failure_scenario: Day/night TOU (day £0.30, night £0.10), DUoS red £0.15 / green £0.005, RTE 0.85. The LP discharges 1 kWh in the red band and, to refill for tomorrow's red window, must charge 1.176 kWh partly in the day band: energy term = 0.30x1.0 - 0.30x1.176 = -£0.053, DUoS term = 0.15x1.0 - 0.005x1.176 = +£0.144. True net £0.091; reported = max(0,-0.053) + 0.144 = £0.144 -> 58% overstated for that cycle. Over 400 MWh/yr of red discharge with day-band charging the deleted loss cost is order £15-20k/yr of FIRM revenue.
findings.consequence: P50 and P90 EBITDA, DSCR, project IRR and equity IRR are all inflated by the deleted charging-loss cost whenever any priced component is negative — a systematic optimistic bias in exactly the FIRM floor a lender relies on.
findings.magnitude: Up to the full flat-rate cost of RTE losses: ~15-18% of discharged kWh x 20-30 p/kWh, order £10-20k/yr per MW-class site; roughly 1-3 pp of project IRR.

findings.title: TariffStack cannot say whether import_rates include DUoS/levies; code stacks DUoS on top unconditionally
findings.defect: TariffStack carries import_rates (label -> £/kWh), separate duos_red/amber/green rates and a separate levies dict, with no field declaring whether the import rates are energy-only or all-in (DUoS/levy-inclusive, the common shape of a GB C&I supplier tariff sheet). Every consumer assumes energy-only: the MILP prices each half-hour as energy_price + duos (milp_solver.py:497 `price = (energy_price if energy_price is not None else np.zeros(n)) + duos`), and the two resulting FIRM streams (TARIFF_ARBITRAGE from the energy component, DUOS_RED_BAND_AVOIDANCE from the DUoS component) are summed into the priced floor. The customer bill likewise adds levies on top (customer_bill.py docstring: 'time-of-use energy + DUoS unit rates + £/kWh levy lines'). If a site's import_rates were transcribed from an inclusive tariff, the red-band premium is counted twice — once inside the day-rate spread, once as duos_red_rate — and the schema cannot even represent the distinction, let alone validate it.
findings.evidence: schemas/tariff.py:14-15 documents only 'map a label ... to a £/kWh value. Rates are non-negative' — no inclusivity basis; tariff.py:21 `import_rates: dict[str, float]` and :23-25 duos_* fields coexist unconditionally; optimisation/milp_solver.py:497 adds DUoS on top of the import-rate series; finance/cashflows.py:585 sums both resulting FIRM streams into the floor.
findings.failure_scenario: A site whose supplier day rate (30p) already embeds ~1.5p amber + red-window DUoS pass-through is entered with duos_red_rate=0.15 from the DNO statement. The dispatch price double-counts the red premium, the optimiser over-values red discharge, and the floor books both an arbitrage stream priced off the inclusive spread and a DUoS-avoidance stream priced off the full red rate: for 400 MWh/yr of red-band discharge that is up to 0.15 x 400,000 = £60k/yr of phantom FIRM revenue.
findings.consequence: Double-counted red-band value in the FIRM floor -> inflated P50/P90, DSCR and IRR; the model is more precise than its input basis justifies and no validator can catch it because the basis is unrepresentable.
findings.magnitude: Up to the full DUoS red rate x red-band discharge volume — tens of £k/yr; several pp of IRR on a small project.
findings.fix: Add a required basis declaration to TariffStack (e.g. import_rates_basis: enum {energy_only_excl_duos_levies, all_in} with no default for new records, defaulting historical records to the code's current assumption energy_only), validate that all_in tariffs do not also carry duos_* rates (or strip them with an explicit warning), and have milp_solver/valuation refuse to stack DUoS onto rates declared all-in. The convention itself is fixed by the existing code (exclusive), so the end state is fully determinable; only re-confirming individual sites' data is an ops task.

findings.title: Per-stream zero-clamping reports more floor revenue than the objective actually earned
findings.defect: The MILP maximises the SUM of the energy and DUoS terms; the valuation then reports each component independently clamped at zero: arbitrage_value_gbp = max(0, energy net) (schedule.py:140), duos_avoidance_value_gbp = max(0, duos net) (schedule.py:145), and _result clamps every stream again (valuation.py:128). max(0,a)+max(0,b) >= a+b, strictly greater whenever one component is negative at the optimum - which the optimiser legitimately produces (e.g. a gap-segmented horizon with no overnight data forces day-band charging for red-band discharge: energy component negative, DUoS component positive, total positive). The code itself acknowledges the signed terms are the true objective (priced_floor_terms_gbp docstring, schedule.py:151-159) but the floor streams that reach finance use the clamped versions.
findings.evidence: schedule.py:140 `return round(max(0.0, self._net_value(self.energy_price_gbp_per_kwh)), 2)`; schedule.py:145 `return round(max(0.0, self._net_value(self.duos_rate_gbp_per_kwh)), 2)`; valuation.py:128 `annual_revenue_gbp=round(max(0.0, revenue), 2)`.
findings.consequence: The FIRM floor total handed to finance exceeds the bill reduction the dispatch actually achieves; P50 revenue is overstated by the absolute value of any negative component.
findings.failure_scenario: Segment covering 07:00-19:00 only (overnight data hole), day 0.30/night 0.10, duos red 0.15/amber 0.03, RTE 0.85. Per kWh red discharge charged in the day band: energy = 0.30x(1-1.176) = -0.053, duos = 0.15-0.03x1.176 = +0.115, true total +0.062 - but reported arbitrage max(0,-0.053)=0 plus DUoS 0.115 = 0.115, an 85% overstatement of that leg.
findings.magnitude: Bounded by the sum of negative component values; zero on clean full-year day/night data, but material (tens of %) on gappy series or amber-charge/red-discharge patterns.
findings.fix: Report the components signed (or clamp only their SUM so it equals the objective's priced-floor terms): assert Sum(stream values) == priced_floor_terms_gbp and allocate any negative component against the positive one before clamping the total at zero.
findings.lens: Dispatch valuation + tariffs (turning a schedule into money)

findings.title: Per-stream max(0,·) clamps let reported floor revenue exceed the LP's own optimum
findings.defect: The LP maximises the COMBINED signal Σ(energy+duos)·(discharge−charge)·Δt, but the valuation splits it into two streams and clamps each at zero independently: arbitrage_value_gbp = max(0, net energy component) (schedule.py:140) and duos_avoidance_value_gbp = max(0, net DUoS component) (schedule.py:145), with a second clamp at valuation.py:128 (`annual_revenue_gbp=round(max(0.0, revenue), 2)`). At any optimum that trades one component against the other, the energy component is negative (the round-trip losses are bought at the retail energy rate to capture the DUoS spread), and clamping it to £0 deletes that cost from the revenue stack. Since clamp(a)+clamp(b) ≥ a+b, the sum of the two FIRM streams handed to finance systematically exceeds the actual bill reduction the LP achieved. The author knew the clamps distort sums — priced_floor_terms_gbp (schedule.py:150-164) exists precisely because the export delta needs the UNCLAMPED terms — but finance's revenue_by_stream reads the clamped per-stream values.
findings.evidence: schedule.py:140 `return round(max(0.0, self._net_value(self.energy_price_gbp_per_kwh)), 2)`; schedule.py:145 `return round(max(0.0, self._net_value(self.duos_rate_gbp_per_kwh)), 2)`; valuation.py:128 `annual_revenue_gbp=round(max(0.0, revenue), 2)`; schedule.py:157-159 docstring admits the per-component values are 'each clamped at £0' and the true delta 'needs the true signed objective terms'.
findings.failure_scenario: Day/night tariff night 28p / day 30p, DUoS red 6p / green 0.3p, RTE 0.85, 365 MWh/yr discharged in red. Energy component = 0.30×365,000 − 0.28×429,412 = −£10,735 (clamped to £0). DUoS component = +£20,612. Reported floor = £0 + £20,612 = £20,612/yr; true LP optimum = £9,877/yr. Reported revenue is 2.09× the value the optimiser itself computed. The CustomerBill on the same QuoteRecord (computed unclamped, schedule.py:229-247) shows the true ~£9.9k saving — the quote contradicts itself.
findings.consequence: P50 revenue, IRR and DSCR are computed on a floor total that can be more than double the LP's own objective value; the customer bill on the same quote shows a different, smaller number.
findings.magnitude: In the worked example +£10,735/yr (+108% of true floor revenue); generally = |negative component|, i.e. the retail cost of round-trip losses.
findings.fix: Report the signed decomposition so the streams sum to the LP objective: keep the DUoS component as revenue and carry a negative energy component as annual_cost_gbp on the tariff-arbitrage stream (the ValueStreamResult already has an annual_cost_gbp field, and dispatch_cost_total already flows priced-floor costs into finance, cashflows.py:647-652). Clamp only the TOTAL (which the LP guarantees ≥ 0 absent forced provisioning), never the components.
findings.lens: Dispatch MILP formulation (the physics)

findings.title: No plausibility screen on series content: constant or single-day-tiled data earns T2 and a full case

findings.title: Local flex: reserved kW is held OUT of dispatch, yet arbitrage discharge is counted as delivered tender MWh and paid utilisation on top of arbitrage+DUoS

findings.title: Target equity IRR default (12.0 = LOW end) flatters the price/viability verdict; its own note claims the opposite
findings.defect: financing.target_equity_irr_pct is set to 12.0 with the note '12.0 is the LOW end, chosen conservatively (a higher hurdle is harder to clear)' (yaml:209-211) — self-contradictory: the note states the conservative direction is a HIGHER hurdle, then picks the LOWER one. In consumption the direction matters: recommend_price builds the revenue requirement as capex × CRF(target_irr, horizon) + opex (pricing.py:58-59, 168-170) and then tests the resulting £/kWh against the customer's counterfactual import cost (pricing.py:183-192). A lower target IRR lowers the price-to-target and makes the 'exceeds_counterfactual / not commercially viable' flag systematically easier to avoid. Arithmetic: CRF(12%, 15y) = 0.12×1.12^15/(1.12^15−1) = 0.1468 vs CRF(13%, 15y) = 0.1547 — the 12% choice understates the capex share of the revenue requirement by ~5.4%, and by ~10.9% versus the plan's '13%+ for an unproven asset class' quote cited in the same source field (yaml:202).

findings.consequence: The default systematically produces the friendliest defensible price-to-target and viability verdict inside the plan's own quoted band, while the provenance note asserts conservatism — an optimism baked into a default and mislabelled as its opposite.

Any case sitting between the two flips from 'viable' to 'not commercially viable' purely on the low-end default.

findings.title: Percent-vs-fraction conventions collide: gearing_pct accepts 0.7 (meaning 70%) as 0.7%
findings.defect: The schema layer mixes two conventions under the same suffix: DebtAssumptions.gearing_pct is a percent in [0,100] (finance.py:26) while ExportArrangement.aggregator_cut_pct is a fraction in [0,1] (export_arrangement.py:36-43). The overlap region [0,1] is silently valid under both readings, so a gearing entered as a fraction (0.7 for 70%) validates and is consumed as 0.7% — debt principal = capex x 0.007 (debt.py builds principal from gearing/100 semantics; DebtTerms.__post_init__ at debt.py:67-68 accepts anything in [0,100]). rate_pct (finance.py:27) is additionally unbounded above (ge=0 only), so rate_pct=700 validates. No consumer sanity-checks the magnitude.
findings.evidence: schemas/finance.py:26 `gearing_pct: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0, le=100)` vs schemas/export_arrangement.py:36-43 `aggregator_cut_pct ... ge=0, le=1 ... as a fraction in [0, 1]`; finance/debt.py:67-68 `if not 0 <= self.gearing_pct <= 100` accepts 0.7; finance/credit.py:236-238 same [0,100] check on the assumption-supplied gearing.
findings.failure_scenario: An assumptions YAML or injected DebtTerms carries gearing 0.7 (author thinking fraction). Debt = 0.7% of capex: DSCR becomes enormous (covenant trivially passes), equity IRR collapses to approximately the project IRR, and the quote reports a 'passing' covenant computed on a debt structure nobody intended.
findings.consequence: Debt sizing, DSCR and equity IRR silently computed on a x100-understated gearing; the covenant verdict shown to a lender is meaningless.
findings.magnitude: Debt principal wrong by ~x100 in the failure case; equity IRR off by the full leverage effect (several pp).
findings.fix: Standardise one convention across the schema layer (percent, matching the majority) and rename/re-bound the outlier (aggregator_cut_pct -> le=100 percent, or gearing to fraction — pick percent since debt.py, credit.py and the haircut keys all divide by 100), then add a plausibility guard: warn/reject gearing_pct < 1 and rate_pct > 30 as almost-certainly mis-united entries. The consistent end state is fully determined by the existing consumers' /100 arithmetic.

findings.title: Connection-binding detection ignores the auxiliary and provisioning draws the bound actually used
findings.defect: binding_constraints tests charge against headroom = connection_limit_kw - site_load_kw, but the solver's real charge upper bound was min(power, conn_limit - load - aux_kw - prov_addition) (milp_solver.py:518, 537-539). With a parasitic draw or a declared load addition, solved charge sits at the true (lower) bound but never reaches the reconstructed headroom, so 'connection_charge_limit' is never reported as binding even when it binds every night.
findings.evidence: schedule.py:194-197 `headroom = connection_limit_kw - self.site_load_kw; charge_at_headroom = (self.charge_kw + tol >= headroom) & ...` vs milp_solver.py:518 `charge_ub = np.minimum(power, np.maximum(0.0, conn_limit - load - aux_kw))`.
findings.consequence: constraints_binding on the quote record understates connection pressure - an investor-facing diagnostic claims the connection never binds when it does, hiding the case for MIC uplift.
findings.failure_scenario: aux_kw = 20 on a 500 kW connection with 300 kW overnight load: charge is capped at 180 kW every night (binding), but headroom is computed as 200 kW, so charge_at_headroom is false and the constraint is never listed.
findings.magnitude: No direct GBP error; corrupts the binding-constraints verdict shown alongside the numbers.
findings.fix: Pass the solver's actual per-instant charge upper-bound inputs (aux_kw and prov_addition) into binding_constraints and test against conn_limit - load - aux - addition, mirroring milp_solver.py:518/537.

findings.title: Schedule ref/quote hashes bake in sub-tolerance solver placement admitted to be non-unique
findings.defect: The schedule's content hash includes the first 48 half-hours of the charge/discharge profiles rounded to 4 dp (schedule.py:299-300). The solver's own comments concede that where the peak tie-break does not bind, per-slot placement is decided below HiGHS's working tolerances and is 'deterministic per machine, not unique by construction' (milp_solver.py:94-98). Solution values are rounded to 6 dp (833-838), far finer than the admitted non-uniqueness. Identical inputs on a different machine/HiGHS build can therefore produce a different dispatch_schedule_ref and hence a different-looking quote lineage, contradicting the 'deterministic core / traceable numbers' claim at the identity level (the £ aggregates are tie-break-equal, but the hash is not).
findings.evidence: schedule.py:299-300 `"charge_kwh_profile_sha": [round(float(x), 4) for x in self.charge_kw[:48]]`; milp_solver.py:95-97 'per-slot coefficient deltas sit below HiGHS's working tolerances, so placement ... remains solver-chosen: deterministic per machine, not unique by construction'.
findings.failure_scenario: The same site JSON + HH file re-run on a lender's machine with a different HiGHS binary yields a schedule with the same £ but different degenerate placement in the first day; ref() differs; the audit trail shows two 'different' dispatches for identical inputs.
findings.consequence: Cross-machine reproducibility audits of the determinism claim fail at the hash level even when every reported £ matches.
findings.magnitude: No £ impact; trust/auditability impact on the determinism contract.
findings.fix: Hash only quantities that are unique at the optimum (the rounded aggregate £, volumes, spec) or round profile samples at a granularity coarser than the solver tolerance (e.g. 0.1 kW), and pin the HiGHS version into the ref payload.
